import torch
from tensordict import TensorDict

from verl.trainer.ppo.core_algos import agg_loss, compute_value_loss, get_policy_loss_fn, kl_penalty
from verl.utils import tensordict_utils as tu
from verl.utils.dataset.dataset_utils import DatasetPadMode
from verl.utils.metric import AggregationType, Metric
from verl.utils.torch_functional import masked_mean, masked_sum
from verl.workers.config import ActorConfig, CriticConfig
from verl.workers.utils.padding import no_padding_2_padding


def sft_loss(config: ActorConfig, model_output, data: TensorDict, dp_group=None):
    pad_mode = tu.get_non_tensor_data(data=data, key="pad_mode", default=DatasetPadMode.NO_PADDING)
    dp_size = data["dp_size"]
    batch_num_tokens = data["batch_num_tokens"]

    log_prob = model_output["log_probs"]

    if pad_mode == DatasetPadMode.NO_PADDING:
        # log_prob and loss mask are nested tensors of shape [bsz, j1]
        # for each sample, loss mask shape is [1, prompt_length + response_length]
        loss_mask = data["loss_mask"]

        log_prob_flatten = log_prob.values()
        loss_mask_flatten = loss_mask.values()

        # left-shift the loss mask by one token to align with log_prob
        loss_mask_flatten = torch.roll(loss_mask_flatten, shifts=-1, dims=0)

        # NOTE: loss is averaged over all tokens in the batch across all data parallel groups,
        # For FSDP backend, the loss is directly used for backward; while for Megatron backend,
        # the loss should be scaled by `num_microbatches` for pp schedule.
        loss = -masked_sum(log_prob_flatten, loss_mask_flatten) / batch_num_tokens * dp_size
    else:
        response_mask = data["response_mask"].to(bool)
        loss = -masked_sum(log_prob, response_mask) / batch_num_tokens * dp_size

    return loss, {}


def ppo_loss(config: ActorConfig, model_output, data: TensorDict, dp_group=None):
    """Computes ppo loss from model output (log_prob, entropy, values, etc. ) and old_log_probs from data."""
    log_prob = no_padding_2_padding(model_output["log_probs"], data)
    entropy = model_output.get("entropy", None)
    if entropy is not None:
        entropy = no_padding_2_padding(entropy, data)

    # global batch info for loss aggregation
    config.global_batch_info["dp_size"] = data["dp_size"]
    config.global_batch_info["batch_num_tokens"] = data["batch_num_tokens"]
    config.global_batch_info["global_batch_size"] = data["global_batch_size"]
    config.global_batch_info["loss_scale_factor"] = config.loss_scale_factor

    # assumes that if any of the global batch info is set, the policy_loss_fn will
    # normalize using dp_size/global_bsz/global_token; in this case, metric aggregation should be SUM
    # to reflect the mean loss over the global batch
    if (
        data["dp_size"] > 1
        or data["batch_num_tokens"] is not None
        or data["global_batch_size"] is not None
        or config.loss_scale_factor is not None
    ):
        metric_aggregation = AggregationType.SUM
    else:
        metric_aggregation = AggregationType.MEAN

    metrics = {}

    # select fields and convert to padded tensor
    fields = ["response_mask", "old_log_probs", "advantages"]
    if "rollout_is_weights" in data:
        fields.append("rollout_is_weights")
    if "ref_log_prob" in data:
        fields.append("ref_log_prob")
    data = data.select(*fields).to_padded_tensor()

    response_mask = data["response_mask"].to(bool)
    # compute policy loss
    old_log_prob = data["old_log_probs"]
    advantages = data["advantages"]
    rollout_is_weights = data.get("rollout_is_weights", None)

    loss_agg_mode = config.loss_agg_mode

    loss_mode = config.policy_loss.get("loss_mode", "vanilla")

    policy_loss_fn = get_policy_loss_fn(loss_mode)
    pg_loss, pg_metrics = policy_loss_fn(
        old_log_prob=old_log_prob,
        log_prob=log_prob,
        advantages=advantages,
        response_mask=response_mask,
        loss_agg_mode=loss_agg_mode,
        config=config,
        rollout_is_weights=rollout_is_weights,
    )

    # AggregationType.MEAN for pg metrics: assumes policy_loss_fn normalizes by local_bsz/local_tokens
    # Ex: in compute_policy_loss_vanilla, pg_metrics are pg_clipfrac, ppo_kl, pg_clipfrac_lower
    pg_metrics = Metric.from_dict(pg_metrics, aggregation=AggregationType.MEAN)

    metrics.update(pg_metrics)
    metrics["actor/pg_loss"] = Metric(value=pg_loss, aggregation=metric_aggregation)
    policy_loss = pg_loss

    # add entropy loss
    if entropy is not None:
        entropy_loss = agg_loss(
            loss_mat=entropy, loss_mask=response_mask, loss_agg_mode=loss_agg_mode, **config.global_batch_info
        )
        entropy_coeff = config.entropy_coeff
        policy_loss -= entropy_coeff * entropy_loss
        metrics["actor/entropy_loss"] = Metric(value=entropy_loss, aggregation=metric_aggregation)

    # add kl loss
    if config.use_kl_loss:
        ref_log_prob = data["ref_log_prob"]
        # compute kl loss
        kld = kl_penalty(logprob=log_prob, ref_logprob=ref_log_prob, kl_penalty=config.kl_loss_type)
        kl_loss = agg_loss(
            loss_mat=kld, loss_mask=response_mask, loss_agg_mode=config.loss_agg_mode, **config.global_batch_info
        )

        policy_loss += kl_loss * config.kl_loss_coef
        metrics["kl_loss"] = Metric(value=kl_loss, aggregation=metric_aggregation)
        metrics["kl_coef"] = config.kl_loss_coef

    return policy_loss, metrics


def value_loss(config: CriticConfig, model_output, data: TensorDict, dp_group=None):
    """value loss

    Args:
        config: CriticConfig
        model_output: model output from the model
        data: the input to the model
        dp_group: data paralle group

    Returns:
        value loss
    """
    vpreds = no_padding_2_padding(model_output["values"], data)  # (bsz, response_length)

    # Normalize the value loss over the global mini-batch (dp_size / batch_num_tokens /
    # global_batch_size) instead of the local micro-batch, so the accumulated critic gradient is
    # invariant to how the mini-batch is split into micro-batches (as the actor's ppo_loss does).
    dp_size = data["dp_size"]
    batch_num_tokens = data["batch_num_tokens"]
    global_batch_size = data["global_batch_size"]

    # When the loss is normalized over the global batch, each micro-batch contributes a partial sum,
    # so the loss metric must be aggregated with SUM to reflect the global-batch mean.
    if (
        dp_size > 1
        or batch_num_tokens is not None
        or global_batch_size is not None
        or config.loss_scale_factor is not None
    ):
        metric_aggregation = AggregationType.SUM
    else:
        metric_aggregation = AggregationType.MEAN

    # select fields and convert to padded tensor
    data = data.select("values", "returns", "response_mask").to_padded_tensor()
    values = data["values"]
    returns = data["returns"]
    response_mask = data["response_mask"].to(bool)

    vf_loss, vf_clipfrac = compute_value_loss(
        vpreds=vpreds,
        values=values,
        returns=returns,
        response_mask=response_mask,

14	"""
15	Rollout Correction Helper Module
16	
17	This module provides a complete pipeline to address **off-policy issues** in RL training,
18	including:
19	1. Policy mismatch between rollout and training implementations (e.g., vLLM BFloat16 vs FSDP FP32)
20	2. Model update staleness (training on trajectories from older checkpoints)
21	3. General distribution shifts between data collection and training
22	
23	Its core capabilities include computing importance sampling (IS) weights,
24	filtering outlier samples via rejection sampling (RS), and
25	tracking metrics to diagnose and correct off-policy issues.
26	
27	## Core Capabilities
28	1. **Multi-Granularity Aggregation**:
29	   - Importance Sampling (IS):
30	        Token-level
31	        Sequence-level
32	   - Rejection Sampling (RS):
33	        Divergence-based filters (token_k*, seq_sum_k*, seq_mean_k*, seq_max_k*)
34	2. **Memory-Efficient Design**:
35	   - Log-space computations to avoid numerical overflow/underflow.
36	   - Fixed safety bounds (exp(±20)) for stable exponentiation.
37	   - Metrics calculated without large intermediate tensors (prevents CUDA OOM).
38	3. **Comprehensive Metrics Tracking**:
39	   - IS/RS statistics (mean/max/min, effective sample size ESS, rejection rate).
40	   - Off-policy diagnostics (KL divergence, perplexity PPL, log PPL difference, χ² divergence).
41	   - Sequence-level breakdowns (deviation from ideal weights, outlier fraction).
42	
43	## Key Interfaces & Usage
44	- compute_rollout_correction_and_rejection_mask(): compute IS weights + rejection mask.
45	- compute_rollout_correction_weights(): only compute truncated IS weights (for variance
46	  reduction, no outlier rejection).
47	- compute_rollout_rejection_mask(): only filter outliers (for sample cleaning, no IS weight
48	  computation).
49	- compute_offpolicy_metrics(): called by core functions to calculate off-policy diagnostics
50	  (KL/PPL/χ²) — no direct external calls needed.
51	
52	### Integration Notes
53	- Used in `ray_trainer.py` via `compute_rollout_correction_and_add_to_batch()` (batch training pipeline).
54	- Used in `dp_actor.py` for distributed worker computations (distributed training scenarios).
55	- All functions support batch inputs and valid token masking (via `response_mask`).
56	
57	
58	## References
59	- "When Speed Kills Stability: Demystifying RL Collapse from the Training-Inference Mismatch": https://richardli.xyz/rl-collapse
60	- Off-policy RL (theoretical basis for IS): https://fengyao.notion.site/off-policy-rl
61	"""
62	
63	import math
64	from typing import Any, Optional
65	
66	import torch

68	import verl.utils.torch_functional as verl_F
69	from verl.protocol import DataProto

73	# Safety bound to prevent numerical overflow/underflow when exponentiating
74	# exp(20) ≈ 485 million (upper limit for stable weights), exp(-20) ≈ 2e-9 (lower limit)
75	SAFETY_BOUND = 20.0
76	
77	SUPPORTED_ROLLOUT_RS_OPTIONS: set[str] = {
78	    "token_k1",
79	    "token_k2",
80	    "token_k3",

86	    "seq_mean_k3",
87	    "seq_max_k2",
88	    "seq_max_k3",
89	}
90	TOKEN_LEVEL_ROLLOUT_RS_OPTIONS: set[str] = {"token_k1", "token_k2", "token_k3"}
91	
92	
93	def _parse_rollout_is_threshold(threshold_spec: str | float) -> tuple[float, Optional[float]]:
94	    if isinstance(threshold_spec, bool):
95	        raise TypeError(
96	            "rollout_is_threshold must be specified as a float or a string threshold specification, not a boolean."
97	        )
98	    if isinstance(threshold_spec, int | float):
99	        upper = float(threshold_spec)
100	        lower = None
101	    elif isinstance(threshold_spec, str):
102	        spec = threshold_spec.strip()
103	        if not spec:
104	            raise ValueError("rollout_is_threshold must not be an empty string.")
105	        if "_" in spec:
106	            lower_str, upper_str = spec.split("_", 1)
107	            try:
108	                lower = float(lower_str)
109	                upper = float(upper_str)
110	            except ValueError as exc:
111	                raise ValueError(f"Invalid rollout_is_threshold '{threshold_spec}'.") from exc
112	        else:
113	            try:
114	                upper = float(spec)
115	            except ValueError as exc:
116	                raise ValueError(f"Invalid rollout_is_threshold '{threshold_spec}'.") from exc
117	            lower = None
118	    else:
119	        raise TypeError("rollout_is_threshold must be a float or a string threshold specification.")
120	
121	    if upper <= 0:
122	        raise ValueError(f"rollout_is_threshold upper bound must be positive, got {upper}.")
123	    if lower is not None:
124	        if lower <= 0:
125	            raise ValueError(f"rollout_is_threshold lower bound must be positive, got {lower}.")
126	        if lower > upper:
127	            raise ValueError("rollout_is_threshold lower bound must be <= upper bound.")
128	
129	    return upper, lower
130	
131	
132	def _parse_rollout_rs_thresholds(
133	    options: list[str], threshold_spec: Optional[str | float]
134	) -> dict[str, dict[str, Optional[float]]]:
135	    if threshold_spec is None:
136	        raise ValueError("rollout_rs_threshold must be provided for rejection sampling.")
137	
138	    if isinstance(threshold_spec, int | float):
139	        raw_specs: list[str] = [str(threshold_spec)]
140	    elif isinstance(threshold_spec, str):
141	        raw_specs = [part.strip() for part in threshold_spec.split(",") if part.strip()]
142	    else:
143	        raise TypeError("rollout_rs_threshold must be a string or numeric value specifying per-option thresholds.")
144	
145	    if not raw_specs:
146	        raise ValueError("rollout_rs_threshold must contain at least one threshold value.")
147	
148	    if len(raw_specs) not in (1, len(options)):
149	        raise ValueError(
150	            f"rollout_rs_threshold expects either one threshold shared by all options or exactly "
151	            f"{len(options)} thresholds to match the provided rollout_rs options."
152	        )
153	
154	    if len(raw_specs) == 1 and len(options) > 1:
155	        raw_specs = raw_specs * len(options)
156	
157	    thresholds: dict[str, dict[str, Optional[float]]] = {}
158	    for option, spec in zip(options, raw_specs, strict=False):
159	        if option.endswith("k1"):
160	            if "_" in spec:
161	                lower_str, upper_str = spec.split("_", 1)
162	            else:
163	                upper_str = spec
164	                lower_str = str(1.0 / float(upper_str))
165	            try:
166	                lower = float(lower_str)
167	                upper = float(upper_str)
168	            except ValueError as exc:
169	                raise ValueError(f"Invalid numeric threshold '{spec}' for option '{option}'.") from exc
170	            if lower <= 0 or upper <= 0:
171	                raise ValueError(f"Thresholds for option '{option}' must be positive, got {spec}.")
172	            thresholds[option] = {
173	                "lower": lower,
174	                "upper": upper,
175	            }
176	        else:
177	            if "_" in spec:
178	                raise ValueError(
179	                    f"rollout_rs_threshold for option '{option}' must provide a single upper bound "
180	                    f"without '_'. Received '{spec}'."
181	                )
182	            try:
183	                upper = float(spec)
184	            except ValueError as exc:
185	                raise ValueError(f"Invalid numeric threshold '{spec}' for option '{option}'.") from exc
186	            if upper <= 0:
187	                raise ValueError(f"Threshold for option '{option}' must be positive, got {spec}.")
188	            thresholds[option] = {
189	                "lower": None,
190	                "upper": upper,
191	            }
192	    return thresholds
193	
194	
195	def compute_rollout_rejection_mask(
196	    log_ratio: torch.Tensor,
197	    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
198	    rollout_rs: str = "token_k1",
199	    rollout_rs_threshold: Optional[str | float] = None,
200	) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, dict[str, float]]:
201	    """Compute hard trust region mask using divergence estimators.
202	
203	    This function enforces a hard trust region constraint by masking tokens/sequences
204	    where the estimated divergence (between training and rollout policies) exceeds
205	    a threshold. Unlike PPO's soft clipping, this provides a hard boundary.
206	
207	    Multiple rejection criteria can be supplied via a comma separated `rollout_rs` string.
208	    All requested options must pass for a token/sequence to remain valid.
209	
210	    Supported KL divergence-based modes (ideal = 0.0 unless noted):
211	    - "token_k{1,2,3}": Token-level divergences.
212	    - "seq_sum_k{1,2,3}": Sum of token divergences per sequence.
213	    - "seq_mean_k{1,2,3}": Mean of token divergences per sequence.
214	    - "seq_max_k{2,3}": Maximum token divergence per sequence.
215	
216	    Args:
217	        log_ratio: Log ratio of training policy probability to rollout policy probability,
218	            shape (batch_size, seq_length).
219	        response_mask: Binary mask for valid tokens (1=valid, 0=padding),
220	            shape (batch_size, seq_length).
221	        rollout_rs: Comma separated rejection sampling options (e.g. "token_k1,seq_sum_k3").
222	        rollout_rs_threshold: Threshold specification string (required). Provide one entry per
223	            rollout_rs option separated by commas. Each entry must be a positive number.
224	            For K1-style options (``*k1``), specify ``lower_upper`` (e.g. ``"0.1_1.2"``)
225	            to denote lower/upper ratio bounds; other options accept a single upper bound.
226	
227	    Returns:
228	        Tuple containing:
229	            modified_response_mask: Response mask with trust region violations masked (0=rejected),
230	                shape (batch_size, seq_length).
231	            metrics: Dictionary of trust region metrics (all scalars).
232	    """
233	    if rollout_rs is None or not isinstance(rollout_rs, str):
234	        raise ValueError("rollout_rs must be a non-empty string (comma separated for multiple options).")
235	    if rollout_rs_threshold is None:
236	        raise ValueError("rollout_rs_threshold must be provided for rejection sampling.")
237	
238	    if log_ratio.shape[0] == 0:
239	        return response_mask, {}
240	
241	    # rollout_rs supports chained criteria via comma separation (e.g. "token_k1,seq_mean_k3").
242	    #            Every listed option must pass; combined_mask aggregates them via logical AND.
243	    option_modes = [opt.strip() for opt in rollout_rs.split(",") if opt.strip()]
244	    if not option_modes:
245	        raise ValueError("rollout_rs must contain at least one valid option.")
246	
247	    normalized_options: list[str] = []
248	    seen: set[str] = set()
249	    for opt in option_modes:
250	        if opt not in SUPPORTED_ROLLOUT_RS_OPTIONS:
251	            raise ValueError(
252	                f"Invalid rollout_rs option: {opt}. Must be one of {sorted(SUPPORTED_ROLLOUT_RS_OPTIONS)}."
253	            )
254	        if opt not in seen:
255	            normalized_options.append(opt)
256	            seen.add(opt)
257	
258	    threshold_specs = _parse_rollout_rs_thresholds(normalized_options, rollout_rs_threshold)
259	
260	    log_ratio_safe: torch.Tensor = torch.clamp(log_ratio, min=-SAFETY_BOUND, max=SAFETY_BOUND)
261	    token_k1: torch.Tensor = -log_ratio_safe
262	    token_k2: torch.Tensor = 0.5 * log_ratio_safe**2
263	    token_k3: torch.Tensor = torch.exp(log_ratio_safe) - 1.0 - log_ratio_safe
264	
265	    response_mask_bool: torch.Tensor = response_mask.bool()
266	    seq_valid_mask: torch.Tensor = response_mask.sum(dim=-1) > 0
267	    # combined_mask accumulates per-option passes; any failure flips tokens to 0.
268	    combined_mask: torch.Tensor = torch.ones_like(response_mask, dtype=log_ratio.dtype)
269	    metrics: dict[str, float] = {}
270	
271	    def _sequence_sum(values: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
272	        return verl_F.masked_sum(values, response_mask, axis=-1)
273	
274	    def _sequence_mean(values: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
275	        return verl_F.masked_mean(values, response_mask, axis=-1)
276	
277	    def _sequence_max(values: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
278	        mask_bool = response_mask.bool()
279	        neg_inf = torch.tensor(float("-inf"), device=values.device, dtype=values.dtype)
280	        masked_values = values.masked_fill(~mask_bool, neg_inf)
281	        max_values = masked_values.max(dim=-1).values
282	        return torch.where(max_values == neg_inf, torch.zeros_like(max_values), max_values)
283	
284	    for option_name in normalized_options:
285	        thresholds_info = threshold_specs[option_name]
286	        is_k1_option = option_name.endswith("k1")
287	        upper_value = thresholds_info["upper"]
288	        lower_value = thresholds_info["lower"]
289	        apply_lower_threshold = is_k1_option
290	        lower_log: Optional[float] = None
291	        upper_log: Optional[float] = None
292	
293	        if is_k1_option:
294	            if lower_value is None or upper_value is None:
295	                raise ValueError(
296	                    f"rollout_rs_threshold for option '{option_name}' must specify both lower and upper bounds."
297	                )
298	            lower_log = math.log(lower_value)
299	            upper_log = math.log(upper_value)
300	        else:
301	            if upper_value is None:
302	                raise ValueError(f"rollout_rs_threshold for option '{option_name}' must specify an upper bound.")
303	
304	        level = "sequence" if option_name not in TOKEN_LEVEL_ROLLOUT_RS_OPTIONS else "token"
305	
306	        per_token_stat: torch.Tensor
307	        per_sequence_stat: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None
308	        token_keep_bool: torch.Tensor
309	
310	        if option_name == "token_k1":
311	            if lower_log is None:
312	                raise ValueError("Threshold specification for token_k1 must include lower and upper bounds.")
313	            per_token_stat = token_k1
314	            token_keep_bool = (per_token_stat >= lower_log) & (per_token_stat <= upper_log)
315	        elif option_name == "token_k2":
316	            per_token_stat = token_k2
317	            token_keep_bool = per_token_stat <= upper_value
318	        elif option_name == "token_k3":
319	            per_token_stat = token_k3
320	            token_keep_bool = per_token_stat <= upper_value
321	        elif option_name.startswith("seq_sum"):
322	            if option_name.endswith("k1"):
323	                if lower_log is None:
324	                    raise ValueError(
325	                        f"Threshold specification for option '{option_name}' must include lower and upper bounds."
326	                    )
327	                seq_stat = _sequence_sum(token_k1)
328	                seq_keep_bool_direct = (seq_stat >= lower_log) & (seq_stat <= upper_log)
329	            elif option_name.endswith("k2"):
330	                seq_stat = _sequence_sum(token_k2)
331	                seq_keep_bool_direct = seq_stat <= upper_value
332	            elif option_name.endswith("k3"):
333	                seq_stat = _sequence_sum(token_k3)
334	                seq_keep_bool_direct = seq_stat <= upper_value
335	            else:
336	                raise ValueError(f"Unsupported rollout_rs option: {option_name}.")
337	            per_sequence_stat = seq_stat
338	            token_keep_bool = seq_keep_bool_direct.unsqueeze(-1).expand_as(response_mask_bool)
339	            per_token_stat = seq_stat.unsqueeze(-1).expand_as(response_mask)
340	        elif option_name.startswith("seq_mean"):
341	            if option_name.endswith("k1"):
342	                if lower_log is None:
343	                    raise ValueError(
344	                        f"Threshold specification for option '{option_name}' must include lower and upper bounds."
345	                    )
346	                seq_stat = _sequence_mean(token_k1)
347	                seq_keep_bool_direct = (seq_stat >= lower_log) & (seq_stat <= upper_log)
348	            elif option_name.endswith("k2"):
349	                seq_stat = _sequence_mean(token_k2)
350	                seq_keep_bool_direct = seq_stat <= upper_value
351	            elif option_name.endswith("k3"):
352	                seq_stat = _sequence_mean(token_k3)
353	                seq_keep_bool_direct = seq_stat <= upper_value
354	            else:
355	                raise ValueError(f"Unsupported rollout_rs option: {option_name}.")
356	            per_sequence_stat = seq_stat
357	            token_keep_bool = seq_keep_bool_direct.unsqueeze(-1).expand_as(response_mask_bool)
358	            per_token_stat = seq_stat.unsqueeze(-1).expand_as(response_mask)
359	        elif option_name.startswith("seq_max"):
360	            if option_name.endswith("k2"):
361	                seq_stat = _sequence_max(token_k2)
362	                seq_keep_bool_direct = seq_stat <= upper_value
363	            elif option_name.endswith("k3"):
364	                seq_stat = _sequence_max(token_k3)
365	                seq_keep_bool_direct = seq_stat <= upper_value
366	            else:
367	                raise ValueError(f"Unsupported rollout_rs option: {option_name}.")
368	            per_sequence_stat = seq_stat
369	            token_keep_bool = seq_keep_bool_direct.unsqueeze(-1).expand_as(response_mask_bool)
370	            per_token_stat = seq_stat.unsqueeze(-1).expand_as(response_mask)
371	        else:
372	            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported rollout_rs option: {option_name}.")
373	
374	        metrics_upper_threshold = upper_log if is_k1_option else upper_value
375	        metrics_lower_threshold = lower_log if (is_k1_option and lower_log is not None) else 0.0
376	
377	        token_keep_mask = token_keep_bool.to(dtype=log_ratio.dtype)
378	        combined_mask = combined_mask * token_keep_mask
379	        seq_keep_bool_tensor = (~((~token_keep_bool) & response_mask_bool)).all(dim=-1)
380	
381	        option_metrics = compute_rs_metrics(
382	            option_name=option_name,
383	            rs_statistic=per_token_stat,
384	            response_mask=response_mask,
385	            seq_valid_mask=seq_valid_mask,
386	            level=level,
387	            per_sequence_values=per_sequence_stat,
388	            rollout_rs_threshold=metrics_upper_threshold,
389	            rollout_rs_threshold_lower=metrics_lower_threshold,
390	            apply_lower_threshold=apply_lower_threshold,
391	        )
392	        metrics.update(option_metrics)
393	
394	        token_masked_fraction = verl_F.masked_mean(1 - token_keep_mask, response_mask).item()
395	        seq_valid_float = seq_valid_mask.float()
396	        if seq_valid_float.sum() > 0:
397	            seq_keep_float = seq_keep_bool_tensor.to(dtype=log_ratio.dtype)
398	            seq_masked_fraction = (((1.0 - seq_keep_float) * seq_valid_float).sum() / seq_valid_float.sum()).item()

404	    final_mask = combined_mask
405	    metrics["rollout_rs_masked_fraction"] = verl_F.masked_mean(1 - final_mask, response_mask).item()
406	    final_keep_bool = (final_mask > 0.5) & response_mask_bool
407	    seq_has_masked: torch.Tensor = (~final_keep_bool & response_mask_bool).any(dim=-1)
408	    metrics["rollout_rs_seq_masked_fraction"] = seq_has_masked.float().mean().item()
409	
410	    modified_response_mask: torch.Tensor = (response_mask * final_mask).to(dtype=response_mask.dtype)
411	    return modified_response_mask, metrics

414	def compute_rs_metrics(
415	    option_name: str,
416	    rs_statistic: torch.Tensor,
417	    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
418	    seq_valid_mask: torch.Tensor,
419	    *,
420	    level: str,
421	    per_sequence_values: Optional[torch.Tensor],
422	    rollout_rs_threshold: float,
423	    rollout_rs_threshold_lower: float,
424	    apply_lower_threshold: bool,
425	) -> dict[str, float]:
426	    """Compute metrics for hard trust region enforcement (per-option).
427	
428	    Args:
429	        option_name: Original option string supplied by the user.
430	        rs_statistic: Trust region statistic (per token) used for thresholding.
431	        response_mask: Binary mask for valid tokens (1=valid, 0=padding).
432	        seq_valid_mask: Boolean mask indicating sequences with at least one valid token.
433	        level: "token" or "sequence" describing aggregation level.
434	        per_sequence_values: Optional per-sequence statistic (same semantics as rs_statistic).
435	        rollout_rs_threshold: Upper threshold.
436	        rollout_rs_threshold_lower: Lower threshold (ignored if ``apply_lower_threshold`` is False).
437	        apply_lower_threshold: Whether to mask/log metrics for values below the lower threshold.
438	    """
439	    if not response_mask.any():
440	        raise ValueError("response_mask must contain at least one valid token (1).")
441	
442	    metrics: dict[str, float] = {}
443	    prefix = f"rollout_rs_{option_name}"
444	    mask_bool: torch.Tensor = response_mask.bool()
445	
446	    # Compute sequence statistics (used by several metrics).
447	    if per_sequence_values is not None:
448	        seq_values = per_sequence_values
449	    else:
450	        seq_values = verl_F.masked_mean(rs_statistic, response_mask, axis=-1)
451	    if seq_values.dim() > 1:
452	        seq_values = seq_values.squeeze(-1)
453	    seq_values_valid = seq_values[seq_valid_mask]
454	
455	    # Mean of the statistic (always reported).
456	    metrics[f"{prefix}_mean"] = verl_F.masked_mean(rs_statistic, response_mask).item()
457	
458	    # Max/min values.
459	    if level == "sequence" and seq_values_valid.numel() > 0:
460	        metrics[f"{prefix}_max"] = seq_values_valid.max().item()
461	        metrics[f"{prefix}_min"] = seq_values_valid.min().item()
462	    else:
463	        metrics[f"{prefix}_max"] = rs_statistic.masked_fill(~mask_bool, float("-inf")).max().item()
464	        metrics[f"{prefix}_min"] = rs_statistic.masked_fill(~mask_bool, float("inf")).min().item()
465	
466	    # Fractions above/below the thresholds.
467	    if level == "sequence" and seq_values_valid.numel() > 0:
468	        fraction_high = (seq_values_valid > rollout_rs_threshold).float().mean().item()
469	        fraction_low = (
470	            (seq_values_valid < rollout_rs_threshold_lower).float().mean().item() if apply_lower_threshold else 0.0
471	        )
472	    else:
473	        fraction_high = verl_F.masked_mean((rs_statistic > rollout_rs_threshold).float(), response_mask).item()
474	        fraction_low = (
475	            verl_F.masked_mean((rs_statistic < rollout_rs_threshold_lower).float(), response_mask).item()
476	            if apply_lower_threshold
477	            else 0.0
478	        )
479	    metrics[f"{prefix}_fraction_high"] = fraction_high
480	    metrics[f"{prefix}_fraction_low"] = fraction_low
481	
482	    # Standard deviation (clamped for stability).
483	    mask_count: torch.Tensor = response_mask.sum()
484	    if mask_count > 1:
485	        if apply_lower_threshold:
486	            clamp_min = rollout_rs_threshold_lower
487	        else:
488	            clamp_min = 0.0
489	        stat_for_std: torch.Tensor = rs_statistic.clamp(min=clamp_min, max=rollout_rs_threshold)
490	        mean_clamped: torch.Tensor = verl_F.masked_mean(stat_for_std, response_mask)
491	        stat_var: torch.Tensor = verl_F.masked_mean(stat_for_std.square(), response_mask) - mean_clamped.square()
492	        metrics[f"{prefix}_std"] = torch.sqrt(torch.clamp(stat_var, min=0.0)).item()
493	    else:
494	        metrics[f"{prefix}_std"] = 0.0
495	
496	    # Sequence-level summary metrics.
497	    if seq_values_valid.numel() > 0:
498	        metrics[f"{prefix}_seq_mean"] = seq_values_valid.mean().item()
499	        metrics[f"{prefix}_seq_std"] = seq_values_valid.std().item() if seq_values_valid.numel() > 1 else 0.0
500	        metrics[f"{prefix}_seq_max"] = seq_values_valid.max().item()
501	        metrics[f"{prefix}_seq_min"] = seq_values_valid.min().item()
502	        metrics[f"{prefix}_seq_max_deviation"] = (seq_values_valid - 0.0).abs().max().item()
503	        metrics[f"{prefix}_seq_fraction_high"] = (seq_values_valid > rollout_rs_threshold).float().mean().item()
504	        if apply_lower_threshold:
505	            metrics[f"{prefix}_seq_fraction_low"] = (
506	                (seq_values_valid < rollout_rs_threshold_lower).float().mean().item()
507	            )
508	    else:
509	        metrics[f"{prefix}_seq_mean"] = 0.0
510	        metrics[f"{prefix}_seq_std"] = 0.0
511	        metrics[f"{prefix}_seq_max"] = 0.0
512	        metrics[f"{prefix}_seq_min"] = 0.0
513	        metrics[f"{prefix}_seq_max_deviation"] = 0.0
514	        metrics[f"{prefix}_seq_fraction_high"] = 0.0
515	        metrics[f"{prefix}_seq_fraction_low"] = 0.0
516	
517	    return metrics

520	def compute_rollout_correction_weights(
521	    log_ratio: torch.Tensor,
522	    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
523	    rollout_is: str = "token",
524	    rollout_is_threshold: str | float = 2.0,
525	    rollout_is_batch_normalize: bool = False,
526	) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, dict[str, float]]:
527	    """Compute importance sampling weights to correct for off-policy distribution shifts.
528	
529	    This function calculates IS weights (π_train / π_rollout) using log ratios for numerical stability.
530	    It supports multiple aggregation levels and truncates extreme weights to prevent training instability.
531	
532	    Key design:
533	    - Log-space computations to avoid overflow
534	    - Truncation of extreme weights (TIS: Truncated Importance Sampling)
535	    - Optional batch normalization (normalize to mean=1.0)
536	    - Metrics tracking for weight distribution analysis
537	
538	    Args:
539	        log_ratio: Log ratio of training policy probability to rollout policy probability,
540	            shape (batch_size, seq_length).
541	        response_mask: Binary mask for valid tokens (1=valid, 0=padding),
542	            shape (batch_size, seq_length).
543	        rollout_is: IS weight aggregation level, must be one of:
544	            - "token": Per-token weights (biased, low variance)
545	            - "sequence": Per-sequence weight (product of tokens; unbiased, high variance)
546	        rollout_is_threshold: Threshold specification for IS weights.
547	            - Single float or float-like string: TIS, clamp weights to the upper bound
548	            - "lower_upper" string: IcePop, zero weights outside [lower, upper]
549	        rollout_is_batch_normalize: Whether to normalize IS weights to have mean=1.0 per batch,
550	            default False.
551	
552	    Returns:
553	        Tuple containing:
554	            rollout_is_weights: Truncated IS weights (masked to zero for padding tokens),
555	                shape (batch_size, seq_length). If batch_normalize=True, normalized to mean=1.0.
556	            metrics: Dictionary of IS weight metrics (all scalars), including:
557	                - rollout_is_mean/max/min: Statistic of weights (before batch normalization)
558	                - rollout_is_eff_sample_size: Effective sample size (ESS)
559	                - rollout_is_seq_*: Sequence-level weight statistics
560	                - rollout_is_batch_norm_factor: Normalization factor (only if batch_normalize=True)
561	    """
562	    # Validate input parameters
563	    valid_is_levels = {"token", "sequence"}
564	    if rollout_is not in valid_is_levels:
565	        raise ValueError(f"Invalid rollout_is: {rollout_is}. Must be one of {valid_is_levels}.")
566	    rollout_is_threshold_upper, rollout_is_threshold_lower = _parse_rollout_is_threshold(rollout_is_threshold)
567	    use_icepop = rollout_is_threshold_lower is not None
568	
569	    # Compute IS weights from log ratio (handles different aggregation levels)
570	    if rollout_is == "token":
571	        # Per-token IS weight: exp(log(π_train/π_rollout)) with safety clamp
572	        log_ratio_for_metrics: torch.Tensor = log_ratio
573	        log_ratio_safe: torch.Tensor = torch.clamp(log_ratio, min=-SAFETY_BOUND, max=SAFETY_BOUND)
574	        raw_rollout_is_weights: torch.Tensor = torch.exp(log_ratio_safe)
575	
576	    elif rollout_is == "sequence":
577	        # Sequence-level IS weight: product of token ratios (exp(sum(log ratios)))
578	        log_ratio_sum: torch.Tensor = verl_F.masked_sum(log_ratio, response_mask, axis=-1).unsqueeze(
579	            -1
580	        )  # Shape: (batch_size, 1)
581	        log_ratio_for_metrics = log_ratio_sum
582	
583	        log_ratio_sum_safe: torch.Tensor = torch.clamp(log_ratio_sum, min=-SAFETY_BOUND, max=SAFETY_BOUND)
584	        raw_rollout_is_weights = torch.exp(log_ratio_sum_safe).expand_as(log_ratio)  # Broadcast to sequence length
585	
586	    else:
587	        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported rollout_is: {rollout_is}")
588	
589	    # Zero out weights for padding tokens using response mask
590	    raw_rollout_is_weights = raw_rollout_is_weights * response_mask
591	
592	    # Apply TIS for a single upper bound and IcePop for a lower_upper string.
593	    if not use_icepop:
594	        rollout_is_weights = raw_rollout_is_weights.clamp(max=rollout_is_threshold_upper)
595	    else:
596	        assert rollout_is_threshold_lower is not None
597	        token_kept_mask = (raw_rollout_is_weights >= rollout_is_threshold_lower) & (
598	            raw_rollout_is_weights <= rollout_is_threshold_upper
599	        )
600	        rollout_is_weights = torch.where(
601	            token_kept_mask, raw_rollout_is_weights, torch.zeros_like(raw_rollout_is_weights)
602	        )
603	
604	    # Compute IS weight metrics.
605	    metrics: dict[str, float] = compute_is_metrics(
606	        rollout_is_weights=rollout_is_weights,
607	        raw_rollout_is_weights=raw_rollout_is_weights,
608	        log_ratio_for_metrics=log_ratio_for_metrics,
609	        response_mask=response_mask,
610	        rollout_is=rollout_is,
611	        rollout_is_threshold=rollout_is_threshold_upper,
612	        rollout_is_threshold_lower=rollout_is_threshold_lower,
613	    )
614	    if use_icepop:
615	        assert rollout_is_threshold_lower is not None
616	        oob_mask = (raw_rollout_is_weights < rollout_is_threshold_lower) | (
617	            raw_rollout_is_weights > rollout_is_threshold_upper
618	        )
619	        metrics["rollout_is_oob_ratio"] = verl_F.masked_mean(oob_mask.float(), response_mask).item()
620	
621	    # Detach weights to prevent gradient flow (mathematically required by IS theory)
622	    # IS weights change the measure, not the objective. See §3.2.2 in docs/algo/rollout_corr_math.md
623	    rollout_is_weights = rollout_is_weights.detach()
624	
625	    # Apply batch normalization if requested
626	    if rollout_is_batch_normalize:
627	        # Compute mean based on aggregation level
628	        mask_float = response_mask.to(dtype=rollout_is_weights.dtype)
629	        if rollout_is == "token":
630	            # Token-level: normalize over all token weights
631	            if torch.distributed.is_available() and torch.distributed.is_initialized():
632	                weights_mean = verl_F.distributed_masked_mean(rollout_is_weights, mask_float)
633	            else:
634	                weights_mean = verl_F.masked_mean(rollout_is_weights, response_mask)
635	        elif rollout_is == "sequence":
636	            # Sequence-level: normalize over sequence weights (one weight per sequence)
637	            # For each sequence, compute mean over valid tokens (they all have the same weight)
638	            # then average across sequences
639	            seq_weights = verl_F.masked_mean(rollout_is_weights, response_mask, axis=-1)  # (batch_size,)
640	            seq_mask = (response_mask.sum(dim=-1) > 0).to(dtype=rollout_is_weights.dtype)
641	            if torch.distributed.is_available() and torch.distributed.is_initialized():
642	                weights_mean = verl_F.distributed_masked_mean(seq_weights, seq_mask)
643	            else:
644	                weights_mean = (seq_weights * seq_mask).sum() / seq_mask.sum().clamp_min(1e-8)
645	        else:
646	            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported rollout_is: {rollout_is}")
647	
648	        # Normalize to mean=1.0 (avoid division by zero)
649	        if weights_mean > 1e-8:
650	            rollout_is_weights = rollout_is_weights / weights_mean
651	            metrics["rollout_is_batch_norm_factor"] = weights_mean.item()
652	        else:
653	            metrics["rollout_is_batch_norm_factor"] = 1.0
654	
655	    return rollout_is_weights, metrics
656

658	def compute_is_metrics(
659	    rollout_is_weights: torch.Tensor,
660	    raw_rollout_is_weights: torch.Tensor,
661	    log_ratio_for_metrics: torch.Tensor,
662	    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
663	    rollout_is: str,
664	    rollout_is_threshold: float,
665	    rollout_is_threshold_lower: Optional[float] = None,
666	) -> dict[str, float]:
667	    """Compute comprehensive metrics for truncated importance sampling weights.
668	
669	    This function calculates statistics for the applied IS weights while using the
670	    raw pre-processing weights to diagnose how often ratios exceed the configured bounds.
671	
672	    Args:
673	        rollout_is_weights: Truncated IS weights (π_train / π_rollout),
674	            shape (batch_size, seq_length).
675	        raw_rollout_is_weights: Raw masked IS weights before TIS / IcePop processing,
676	            shape (batch_size, seq_length).
677	        log_ratio_for_metrics: Log ratio of training to rollout probabilities (unclamped),
678	            shape varies by aggregation level.
679	        response_mask: Binary mask for valid tokens (1=valid, 0=padding),
680	            shape (batch_size, seq_length).
681	        rollout_is: IS weight aggregation level (matches compute_rollout_correction_weights).
682	        rollout_is_threshold: Upper threshold for truncated IS weights.
683	
684	    Returns:
685	        Dictionary of IS weight metrics (all scalars).
686	    """
687	    if not response_mask.any():
688	        raise ValueError("response_mask must contain at least one valid token (1).")
689	
690	    metrics: dict[str, float] = {}
691	    device: torch.device = rollout_is_weights.device
692	    # Default lower threshold (reciprocal of upper threshold)
693	    rollout_is_threshold_lower = (
694	        1.0 / rollout_is_threshold if rollout_is_threshold_lower is None else rollout_is_threshold_lower
695	    )
696	
697	    # Precompute log thresholds for accurate checks
698	    log_threshold_upper: torch.Tensor = torch.log(torch.tensor(rollout_is_threshold, device=device))
699	    log_threshold_lower: torch.Tensor = torch.log(torch.tensor(rollout_is_threshold_lower, device=device))
700	
701	    # Compute metrics based on aggregation level
702	    if rollout_is == "sequence":
703	        # Sequence-level aggregation: use log-space for unclamped stats
704	        log_max: torch.Tensor = log_ratio_for_metrics.max()
705	        log_min: torch.Tensor = log_ratio_for_metrics.min()
706	        metrics["rollout_is_max"] = torch.exp(torch.clamp(log_max, max=SAFETY_BOUND)).item()
707	        metrics["rollout_is_min"] = torch.exp(log_min).item()
708	
709	        # Mean uses truncated weights to avoid overflow
710	        metrics["rollout_is_mean"] = verl_F.masked_mean(rollout_is_weights, response_mask).item()
711	
712	        # Fraction of weights exceeding thresholds (log-space for accuracy)
713	        exceeds_upper: torch.Tensor = log_ratio_for_metrics > log_threshold_upper
714	        below_lower: torch.Tensor = log_ratio_for_metrics < log_threshold_lower
715	        metrics["rollout_is_ratio_fraction_high"] = exceeds_upper.float().mean().item()
716	        metrics["rollout_is_ratio_fraction_low"] = below_lower.float().mean().item()
717	
718	    else:  # token-level
719	        # Token-level aggregation: the applied weights drive loss, std, and ESS,
720	        # while high/low fractions are measured from the raw pre-processing weights.
721	        metrics["rollout_is_mean"] = verl_F.masked_mean(rollout_is_weights, response_mask).item()
722	
723	        # Fraction of tokens exceeding thresholds
724	        rollout_is_above_threshold: torch.Tensor = raw_rollout_is_weights > rollout_is_threshold
725	        rollout_is_below_threshold: torch.Tensor = raw_rollout_is_weights < rollout_is_threshold_lower
726	        metrics["rollout_is_ratio_fraction_high"] = verl_F.masked_mean(
727	            rollout_is_above_threshold.float(), response_mask
728	        ).item()
729	        metrics["rollout_is_ratio_fraction_low"] = verl_F.masked_mean(
730	            rollout_is_below_threshold.float(), response_mask
731	        ).item()
732	
733	        # Max/min (mask out padding tokens)
734	        mask_bool: torch.Tensor = response_mask.bool()
735	        metrics["rollout_is_max"] = rollout_is_weights.masked_fill(~mask_bool, float("-inf")).max().item()
736	        metrics["rollout_is_min"] = rollout_is_weights.masked_fill(~mask_bool, float("inf")).min().item()
737	
738	    # Compute standard deviation / ESS from the actual applied weights so exact
739	    # IcePop diagnostics preserve zeroed-out coefficients.
740	    mask_count: torch.Tensor = response_mask.sum()
741	    if mask_count > 1:
742	        weights_for_std: torch.Tensor = rollout_is_weights.clamp(min=0.0, max=rollout_is_threshold)
743	        mean_clamped: torch.Tensor = verl_F.masked_mean(weights_for_std, response_mask)
744	        rollout_is_var: torch.Tensor = (
745	            verl_F.masked_mean(weights_for_std.square(), response_mask) - mean_clamped.square()
746	        )
747	        metrics["rollout_is_std"] = torch.sqrt(torch.clamp(rollout_is_var, min=0.0)).item()
748	    else:
749	        metrics["rollout_is_std"] = 0.0
750	
751	    # Compute Effective Sample Size (ESS) for truncated weights
752	    weights_for_ess: torch.Tensor = rollout_is_weights.clamp(min=0.0, max=rollout_is_threshold)
753	    mean_for_ess: torch.Tensor = verl_F.masked_mean(weights_for_ess, response_mask)
754	    is_weights_normalized: torch.Tensor = weights_for_ess / (mean_for_ess + 1e-8)  # Avoid division by zero
755	    metrics["rollout_is_eff_sample_size"] = (
756	        1.0 / verl_F.masked_mean(is_weights_normalized.square(), response_mask).item()
757	    )
758	
759	    # Add sequence-level metrics if weights have batch dimension
760	    if rollout_is_weights.dim() > 1:
761	        seq_mean_weights: torch.Tensor = verl_F.masked_mean(rollout_is_weights, response_mask, axis=-1)
762	
763	        metrics["rollout_is_seq_mean"] = seq_mean_weights.mean().item()
764	        metrics["rollout_is_seq_std"] = seq_mean_weights.std().item() if seq_mean_weights.numel() > 1 else 0.0
765	        metrics["rollout_is_seq_max"] = seq_mean_weights.max().item()
766	        metrics["rollout_is_seq_min"] = seq_mean_weights.min().item()
767	
768	        # Sequence deviation from ideal weight (1.0)
769	        seq_deviation: torch.Tensor = (seq_mean_weights - 1.0).abs()
770	        metrics["rollout_is_seq_max_deviation"] = seq_deviation.max().item()
771	
772	        # Fraction of sequences with extreme weights. Use the raw (pre-truncation)
773	        # per-sequence mean: every clamped weight is <= rollout_is_threshold, so a mean
774	        # of clamped weights can never exceed it and the high fraction would be dead.
775	        raw_seq_mean_weights: torch.Tensor = verl_F.masked_mean(raw_rollout_is_weights, response_mask, axis=-1)
776	        metrics["rollout_is_seq_fraction_high"] = (raw_seq_mean_weights > rollout_is_threshold).float().mean().item()
777	        metrics["rollout_is_seq_fraction_low"] = (
778	            (raw_seq_mean_weights < rollout_is_threshold_lower).float().mean().item()
779	        )
780	
781	    return metrics
782

784	def compute_rollout_correction_and_rejection_mask(
785	    old_log_prob: torch.Tensor,
786	    rollout_log_prob: torch.Tensor,
787	    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
788	    rollout_is: Optional[str] = None,
789	    rollout_is_threshold: Optional[str | float] = 2.0,
790	    rollout_is_batch_normalize: bool = False,
791	    rollout_rs: Optional[str] = None,
792	    rollout_rs_threshold: Optional[str | float] = None,
793	) -> tuple[Optional[DataProto], torch.Tensor, dict[str, float]]:
794	    """Unified interface for computing IS weights and rejection masks.
795	
796	    This function combines IS weight calculation (truncated) and rejection sampling (masked)
797	    into a single pipeline.
798	
799	    Key design:
800	    - Separation of IS weights (for variance reduction) and rejection masks (for sample filtering)
801	    - Comprehensive metrics tracking for mismatch diagnosis
802	
803	    Args:
804	        old_log_prob: Log probabilities from the training policy (e.g., FSDP FP32),
805	            shape (batch_size, seq_length).
806	        rollout_log_prob: Log probabilities from the rollout policy (e.g., vLLM BF16),
807	            shape (batch_size, seq_length).
808	        response_mask: Binary mask for valid tokens (1=valid, 0=padding),
809	            shape (batch_size, seq_length).
810	        rollout_is: IS weight aggregation level (see compute_rollout_correction_weights for options).
811	            Set to None to disable IS weight computation.
812	        rollout_is_threshold: Threshold specification for IS weights.
813	            Single float implies TIS; "lower_upper" implies IcePop.
814	        rollout_rs: Rejection sampling aggregation modes as a comma separated string
815	            (see compute_rollout_rejection_mask for the full list). Set to None to disable
816	            rejection sampling.
817	        rollout_rs_threshold: Threshold specification string (see compute_rollout_rejection_mask for details).
818	            Provide one threshold per option (comma separated). For K1-style options, specify
819	            ``lower_upper`` to denote the lower/upper ratio bounds.
820	        rollout_is_batch_normalize: Whether to normalize IS weights to have mean=1.0 per batch.
821	            Default: False.
822	
823	    Returns:
824	        Tuple containing:
825	            rollout_is_weights_proto: DataProto with IS weights (None if rollout_is is None),
826	                key "rollout_is_weights", shape (batch_size, seq_length).
827	            modified_response_mask: Response mask with rejection sampling applied,
828	                shape (batch_size, seq_length).
829	            metrics: Dictionary of all metrics (prefixed with "rollout_corr/"), including:
830	                - IS weight statistics
831	                - Rejection sampling rates
832	                - Policy mismatch metrics (KL, PPL, etc.)
833	    """
834	    # Validate input masks
835	    if not response_mask.any():
836	        raise ValueError("response_mask must contain at least one valid token (1).")
837	    if old_log_prob.shape != rollout_log_prob.shape:
838	        raise ValueError(
839	            f"old_log_prob shape {old_log_prob.shape} does not match rollout_log_prob shape {rollout_log_prob.shape}."
840	        )
841	    if old_log_prob.shape != response_mask.shape:
842	        raise ValueError(
843	            f"log_prob shape {old_log_prob.shape} does not match response_mask shape {response_mask.shape}."
844	        )
845	
846	    # Step 1: Compute log ratio (log(π_train / π_rollout))
847	    log_ratio: torch.Tensor = old_log_prob - rollout_log_prob

902	def compute_offpolicy_metrics(
903	    old_log_prob: torch.Tensor,
904	    rollout_log_prob: Optional[torch.Tensor],
905	    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
906	) -> dict[str, Any]:
907	    """Compute off-policy diagnostic metrics (helper function).
908	
909	    This helper function operates on raw tensors and is used internally by:
910	    - compute_rollout_correction_and_rejection_mask() in this module (automatically included)
911	    - Tests (test_rollout_corr.py, test_rollout_corr_integration.py)
912	
913	    These metrics help diagnose the off-policy gap between rollout and training policies,
914	    which can arise from:
915	    - Policy mismatch (e.g., vLLM BF16 vs FSDP FP32)
916	    - Model staleness (training on trajectories from older checkpoints)
917	    - General distribution shifts
918	
919	    Key metrics:
920	    - kl: Direct KL divergence estimator KL(π_rollout || π_training)
921	    - k3_kl: K3 KL estimator for stability (more stable for small KL)
922	    - training_ppl: Perplexity of training policy
923	    - rollout_ppl: Perplexity of rollout policy
924	    - log_ppl_diff: Difference in log perplexities
925	    - ppl_ratio: Ratio of training PPL to rollout PPL
926	    - chi2_token: Token-level χ² divergence E[ρ²] - 1
927	    - chi2_seq: Sequence-level χ² divergence E[(∏ρ_t)²] - 1
928	
929	    Args:
930	        old_log_prob: Log probabilities from training policy, shape (batch_size, seq_length)
931	        rollout_log_prob: Log probabilities from rollout policy, shape (batch_size, seq_length)
932	        response_mask: Mask for valid tokens, shape (batch_size, seq_length)
933	
934	    Returns:
935	        Dictionary of off-policy metrics (without prefix)
936	    """
937	    # Validate that we have at least one valid token
938	    assert response_mask.any(), "Expected at least one valid token in response_mask"
939	
940	    metrics = {}
941	
942	    # 1. Training policy perplexity (always available)
943	    # Formula: exp(-1/|T| * Σ log π_training(y_t|y_<t))
944	    # where |T| is the number of tokens generated by the model
945	    mean_log_prob_training = verl_F.masked_mean(old_log_prob, response_mask, axis=-1)  # (batch_size,)
946	    training_ppl = torch.exp(-mean_log_prob_training).mean()  # Batch mean of per-sequence PPL
947	    metrics["training_ppl"] = training_ppl.detach().item()
948	
949	    # Also log log-ppl for easier analysis (avoids exponential scale)
950	    metrics["training_log_ppl"] = (-mean_log_prob_training).mean().detach().item()
951	
952	    # 2. Compute rollout off-policy metrics (only if rollout_log_probs available)
953	    if rollout_log_prob is not None:
954	        # 2a. kl: Direct estimator for KL(π_rollout || π_training)
955	        # This is the standard KL divergence: E[log(π_rollout) - log(π_training)]
956	        # Positive value means rollout policy is more confident than training policy
957	        metrics["kl"] = verl_F.masked_mean(rollout_log_prob - old_log_prob, response_mask).detach().item()
958	
959	        # 2b. k3_kl: K3 estimator for KL(π_rollout || π_training)
960	        # More stable for small KL values using: E[exp(log_ratio) - log_ratio - 1]
961	        # Formula: KL ≈ E[r - log(r) - 1] where r = π_training/π_rollout
962	        log_ratio = old_log_prob - rollout_log_prob
963	        k3_kl_matrix = torch.exp(log_ratio) - log_ratio - 1
964	        metrics["k3_kl"] = verl_F.masked_mean(k3_kl_matrix, response_mask).detach().item()
965	
966	        # 2c. Rollout policy perplexity
967	        mean_log_prob_rollout = verl_F.masked_mean(rollout_log_prob, response_mask, axis=-1)  # (batch_size,)
968	        rollout_ppl = torch.exp(-mean_log_prob_rollout).mean()  # Batch mean of per-sequence PPL
969	        metrics["rollout_ppl"] = rollout_ppl.detach().item()
970	        metrics["rollout_log_ppl"] = (-mean_log_prob_rollout).mean().detach().item()
971	
972	        # 2d. Log PPL difference (sequence-level perplexity difference)
973	        # log_ppl_diff = mean_log_prob_rollout - mean_log_prob_training
974	        # Since ppl = exp(-log_prob), we have:
975	        #   log(ppl_ratio) = log(training_ppl/rollout_ppl) = log_ppl_diff
976	        # Positive value means training assigns lower probability (higher PPL) than rollout
977	        log_ppl_diff = mean_log_prob_rollout - mean_log_prob_training
978	        metrics["log_ppl_diff"] = log_ppl_diff.mean().detach().item()
979	        metrics["log_ppl_abs_diff"] = log_ppl_diff.abs().mean().detach().item()
980	        metrics["log_ppl_diff_max"] = log_ppl_diff.max().detach().item()
981	        metrics["log_ppl_diff_min"] = log_ppl_diff.min().detach().item()
982	
983	        # 2e. PPL ratio (how much higher is training PPL vs rollout PPL)
984	        # Compute per-sequence ratio first, then average
985	        # For numerical stability, compute in log space using log_ppl_diff
986	        # Note: log_ppl_diff = log(ppl_ratio), so ppl_ratio = exp(log_ppl_diff)
987	        # This is the inverse of geometric IS: ppl_ratio_i = 1 / geometric_is_i for each sequence
988	        ppl_ratio = torch.exp(log_ppl_diff).mean()  # mean(exp(log_ppl_diff)) = mean(ppl_ratio_i)
989	        metrics["ppl_ratio"] = ppl_ratio.detach().item()
990	
991	        # 2f. Chi-squared divergence: χ²(π_training || π_rollout) = E_μ[ρ²] - 1
992	        # where ρ = π_training / π_rollout and μ = π_rollout (rollout distribution)
993	        # This measures the variance of importance sampling weights
994	        # Token-level: E_token[ρ²] - 1 (averaged over all tokens)
995	        log_ratio_safe = torch.clamp(log_ratio, min=-SAFETY_BOUND, max=SAFETY_BOUND)
996	        rho_token = torch.exp(log_ratio_safe)  # ρ = π_training / π_rollout (token-level)
997	        rho_squared_token = rho_token.square()
998	        chi2_token = verl_F.masked_mean(rho_squared_token, response_mask) - 1.0
999	        metrics["chi2_token"] = chi2_token.detach().item()
1000	
1001	        # Sequence-level: E_seq[(Π ρ_t)²] - 1 = E_seq[exp(2 * Σ log ρ_t)] - 1
1002	        log_ratio_sum = verl_F.masked_sum(log_ratio, response_mask, axis=-1)  # Σ log ρ_t per sequence
1003	        log_ratio_sum_safe = torch.clamp(log_ratio_sum, min=-SAFETY_BOUND, max=SAFETY_BOUND)
1004	        rho_squared_seq = torch.exp(2.0 * log_ratio_sum_safe)  # (Π ρ_t)²
1005	        chi2_seq = rho_squared_seq.mean() - 1.0
1006	        metrics["chi2_seq"] = chi2_seq.detach().item()
1007	
1008	    return metrics

Precompute log thresholds for accurate checks\n    log_threshold_upper: torch.Tensor = torch.log(torch.tensor(rollout_is_threshold, device=device))\n    log_threshold_lower: torch.Tensor = torch.log(torch.tensor(rollout_is_threshold_lower, device=device))\n\n    # Compute metrics based on aggregation level\n    if rollout_is == \"sequence\":\n        # Sequence-level aggregation: use log-space for unclamped stats\n        log_max: torch.Tensor = log_ratio_for_metrics.max()\n        log_min: torch.Tensor = log_ratio_for_metrics.min()\n        metrics[\"rollout_is_max\"] = torch.exp(torch.clamp(log_max, max=SAFETY_BOUND)).item()\n        metrics[\"rollout_is_min\"] = torch.exp(log_min).item()\n\n        # Mean uses truncated weights to avoid overflow\n        metrics[\"rollout_is_mean\"] = verl_F.masked_mean(rollout_is_weights, response_mask).item()\n\n        # Fraction of weights exceeding thresholds (log-space for accuracy)\n        exceeds_upper: torch.Tensor = log_ratio_for_metrics > log_threshold_upper\n        below_lower: torch.Tensor = log_ratio_for_metrics < log_threshold_lower\n        metrics[\"rollout_is_ratio_fraction_high\"] = exceeds_upper.float().mean().item()\n        metrics[\"rollout_is_ratio_fraction_low\"] = below_lower.float().mean().item()\n\n    else:  # token-level\n        # Token-level aggregation: the applied weights drive loss, std, and ESS,\n        # while high/low fractions are measured from the raw pre-processing weights.\n        metrics[\"rollout_is_mean\"] = verl_F.masked_mean(rollout_is_weights, response_mask).item()\n\n        # Fraction of tokens exceeding thresholds\n        rollout_is_above_threshold: torch.Tensor = raw_rollout_is_weights > rollout_is_threshold\n        rollout_is_below_threshold: torch.Tensor = raw_rollout_is_weights < rollout_is_threshold_lower\n        metrics[\"rollout_is_ratio_fraction_high\"] = verl_F.masked_mean(\n            rollout_is_above_threshold.float(), response_mask\n        ).item()\n        metrics[\"rollout_is_ratio_fraction_low\"] = verl_F.masked_mean(\n            rollout_is_below_threshold.float(), response_mask\n        ).item()\n\n        # Max/min (mask out padding tokens)\n        mask_bool: torch.Tensor = response_mask.bool()\n        metrics[\"rollout_is_max\"] = rollout_is_weights.masked_fill(~mask_bool, float(\"-inf\")).max().item()\n        metrics[\"rollout_is_min\"] = rollout_is_weights.masked_fill(~mask_bool, float(\"inf\")).min().item()\n\n    # Compute standard deviation / ESS from the actual applied weights so exact\n    # IcePop diagnostics preserve zeroed-out coefficients.\n    mask_count: torch.Tensor = response_mask.sum()\n    if mask_count > 1:\n        weights_for_std: torch.Tensor = rollout_is_weights.clamp(min=0.0, max=rollout_is_threshold)\n        mean_clamped: torch.Tensor = verl_F.masked_mean(weights_for_std, response_mask)\n        rollout_is_var: torch.Tensor = (\n            verl_F.masked_mean(weights_for_std.square(), response_mask) - mean_clamped.square()\n        )\n        metrics[\"rollout_is_std\"] = torch.sqrt(torch.clamp(rollout_is_var, min=0.0)).item()\n    else:\n        metrics[\"rollout_is_std\"] = 0.0\n\n    # Compute Effective Sample Size (ESS) for truncated weights\n    weights_for_ess: torch.Tensor = rollout_is_weights.clamp(min=0.0, max=rollout_is_threshold)\n    mean_for_ess: torch.Tensor = verl_F.masked_mean(weights_for_ess, response_mask)\n    is_weights_normalized: torch.Tensor = weights_for_ess / (mean_for_ess + 1e-8)  # Avoid division by zero\n    metrics[\"rollout_is_eff_sample_size\"] = (\n        1.0 / verl_F.masked_mean(is_weights_normalized.square(), response_mask).item()\n    )\n\n    # Add sequence-level metrics if weights have batch dimension\n    if rollout_is_weights.dim() > 1:\n        seq_mean_weights: torch.Tensor = verl_F.masked_mean(rollout_is_weights, response_mask, axis=-1)\n\n        metrics[\"rollout_is_seq_mean\"] = seq_mean_weights.mean().item()\n        metrics[\"rollout_is_seq_std\"] = seq_mean_weights.std().item() if seq_mean_weights.numel() > 1 else 0.0\n        metrics[\"rollout_is_seq_max\"] = seq_mean_weights.max().item()\n        metrics[\"rollout_is_seq_min\"] = seq_mean_weights.min().item()\n\n        # Sequence deviation from ideal weight (1.0)\n        seq_deviation: torch.Tensor = (seq_mean_weights - 1.0).abs()\n        metrics[\"rollout_is_seq_max_deviation\"] = seq_deviation.max().item()\n\n        # Fraction of sequences with extreme weights. Use the raw (pre-truncation)\n        # per-sequence mean: every clamped weight is <= rollout_is_threshold, so a mean\n        # of clamped weights can never exceed it and the high fraction would be dead.\n        raw_seq_mean_weights: torch.Tensor = verl_F.masked_mean(raw_rollout_is_weights, response_mask, axis=-1)\n        metrics[\"rollout_is_seq_fraction_high\"] = (raw_seq_mean_weights > rollout_is_threshold).float().mean().item()\n        metrics[\"rollout_is_seq_fraction_low\"] = (\n            (raw_seq_mean_weights < rollout_is_threshold_lower).float().mean().item()\n        )\n\n    return metrics\n\n\ndef compute_rollout_correction_and_rejection_mask(\n    old_log_prob: torch.Tensor,\n    rollout_log_prob: torch.Tensor,\n    response_mask: torch.Tensor,\n    rollout_is: Optional[str] = None,\n    rollout_is_threshold: Optional[str | float] = 2.0,\n    rollout_is_batch_normalize: bool = False,\n    rollout_rs: Optional[str] = None,\n    rollout_rs_threshold: Optional[str | float] = None,\n) -> tuple[Optional[DataProto], torch.Tensor, dict[str, float]]:\n    \"\"\"Unified interface for computing IS weights and rejection masks.\n\n    This function combines IS weight calculation (truncated) and rejection sampling (masked)\n    into a single pipeline.\n\n    Key design:\n    - Separation of IS weights (for variance reduction) and rejection masks (for sample filtering)\n    - Comprehensive metrics tracking for mismatch diagnosis\n\n    Args:\n        old_log_prob: Log probabilities from the training policy (e.g., FSDP FP32),\n            shape (batch_size, seq_length).\n        rollout_log_prob: Log probabilities from the rollout policy (e.g., vLLM BF16),\n            shape (batch_size, seq_length).\n        response_mask: Binary mask for valid tokens (1=valid, 0=padding),\n            shape (batch_size, seq_length).\n        rollout_is: IS weight aggregation level (see compute_rollout_correction_weights for options).\n            Set to None to disable IS weight computation.\n        rollout_is_threshold: Threshold specification for IS weights.\n            Single float implies TIS; \"lower_upper\" implies IcePop.\n        rollout_rs: Rejection sampling aggregation modes as a comma separated string\n            (see compute_rollout_rejection_mask for the full list). Set to None to disable\n            rejection sampling.\n        rollout_rs_threshold: Threshold specification string (see compute_rollout_rejection_mask for details).\n            Provide one threshold per option (comma separated). For K1-style options, specify\n            ``lower_upper`` to denote the lower/upper ratio bounds.\n        rollout_is_batch_normalize: Whether to normalize IS weights to have mean=1.0 per batch.\n            Default: False.\n\n    Returns:\n        Tuple containing:\n            rollout_is_weights_proto: DataProto with IS weights (None if rollout_is is None),\n                key \"rollout_is_weights\", shape (batch_size, seq_length).\n            modified_response_mask: Response mask with rejection sampling applied,\n                shape (batch_size, seq_length).\n            metrics: Dictionary of all metrics (prefixed with \"rollout_corr/\"), including:\n                - IS weight statistics\n                - Rejection sampling rates\n                - Policy mismatch metrics (KL, PPL, etc.)\n    \"\"\"\n    # Validate input masks\n    if not response_mask.any():\n        raise ValueError(\"response_mask must contain at least one valid token (1).\")\n    if old_log_prob.shape != rollout_log_prob.shape:\n        raise ValueError(\n            f\"old_log_prob shape {old_log_prob.shape} does not match rollout_log_prob shape {rollout_log_prob.shape}.\"\n        )\n    if old_log_prob.shape != response_mask.shape:\n        raise ValueError(\n            f\"log_prob shape {old_log_prob.shape} does not match response_mask shape {response_mask.shape}.\"\n        )\n\n    # Step 1: Compute log ratio (log(π_train / π_rollout))\n    log_ratio: torch.Tensor = old_log_prob - rollout_log_prob\n    metrics: dict[str, float] = {}\n\n    # Step 2: Compute IS weights (if enabled)\n    rollout_is_weights: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None\n    if rollout_is is not None and rollout_is_threshold is not None:\n        rollout_is_weights, is_metrics = compute_rollout_correction_weights(\n            log_ratio=log_ratio,\n            response_mask=response_mask,\n            rollout_is=rollout_is,\n            rollout_is_threshold=rollout_is_threshold,\n            rollout_is_batch_normalize=rollout_is_batch_normalize,\n        )\n        metrics.update(is_metrics)\n\n    # Step 3: Compute rejection mask (if enabled)\n    modified_response_mask: torch.Tensor = response_mask.clone()\n    if rollout_rs is not None:\n        if rollout_rs_threshold is None:\n            raise ValueError(\n                \"rollout_rs_threshold must be explicitly provided when rollout_rs is enabled. \"\n                \"Set rollout_rs_threshold to the desired threshold value.\"\n            )\n        modified_response_mask, rs_metrics = compute_rollout_rejection_mask(\n            log_ratio=log_ratio,\n            response_mask=response_mask,\n            rollout_rs=rollout_rs,\n            rollout_rs_threshold=rollout_rs_threshold,\n        )\n        metrics.update(rs_metrics)\n\n    # Step 4: Compute off-policy metrics (KL, PPL, χ², etc.)\n    offpolicy_metrics: dict[str, float] = compute_offpolicy_metrics(\n        old_log_prob=old_log_prob,\n        rollout_log_prob=rollout_log_prob,\n        response_mask=response_mask,\n    )\n    metrics.update(offpolicy_metrics)\n\n    # Step 6: Add \"rollout_corr/\" prefix to all metrics for logging consistency\n    metrics_scalar: dict[str, float] = {}\n    for key, value in metrics.items():\n        if isinstance(value, torch.Tensor):\n            metrics_scalar[f\"rollout_corr/{key}\"] = value.item()\n        else:\n            metrics_scalar[f\"rollout_corr/{key}\"] = value\n\n    # Step 7: Wrap IS weights in DataProto for consistency with API\n    rollout_is_weights_proto: Optional[DataProto] = None\n    if rollout_is_weights is not None:\n        rollout_is_weights_proto = DataProto.from_dict(tensors={\"rollout_is_weights\": rollout_is_weights})\n\n    return rollout_is_weights_proto, modified_response_mask, metrics_scalar\n\n\ndef compute_offpolicy_metrics(\n    old_log_prob: torch.Tensor,\n    rollout_log_prob: Optional[torch.Tensor],\n    response_mask: torch.Tensor,\n) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"Compute off-policy diagnostic metrics (helper function).\n\n    This helper function operates on raw tensors and is used internally by:\n    - compute_rollout_correction_and_rejection_mask() in this module (automatically included)\n    - Tests (test_rollout_corr.py, test_rollout_corr_integration.py)\n\n    These metrics help diagnose the off-policy gap between rollout and training policies,\n    which can arise from:\n    - Policy mismatch (e.g., vLLM BF16 vs FSDP FP32)\n    - Model staleness (training on trajectories from older checkpoints)\n    - General distribution shifts\n\n    Key metrics:\n    - kl: Direct KL divergence estimator KL(π_rollout || π_training)\n    - k3_kl: K3 KL estimator for stability (more stable for small KL)\n    - training_ppl: Perplexity of training policy\n    - rollout_ppl: Perplexity of rollout policy\n    - log_ppl_diff: Difference in log perplexities\n    - ppl_ratio: Ratio of training PPL to rollout PPL\n    - chi2_token: Token-level χ² divergence E[ρ²] - 1\n    - chi2_seq: Sequence-level χ² divergence E[(∏ρ_t)²] - 1\n\n    Args:\n        old_log_prob: Log probabilities from training policy, shape (batch_size, seq_length)\n        rollout_log_prob: Log probabilities from rollout policy, shape (batch_size, seq_length)\n        response_mask: Mask for valid tokens, shape (batch_size, seq_length)\n\n    Returns:\n        Dictionary of off-policy metrics (without prefix)\n    \"\"\"\n    # Validate that we have at least one valid token\n    assert response_mask.any(), \"Expected at least one valid token in response_mask\"\n\n    metrics = {}\n\n    # 1. Training policy perplexity (always available)\n    # Formula: exp(-1/|T| * Σ log π_training(y_t|y_<t))\n    # where |T| is the number of tokens generated by the model\n    mean_log_prob_training = verl_F.masked_mean(old_log_prob, response_mask, axis=-1)  # (batch_size,)\n    training_ppl = torch.exp(-mean_log_prob_training).mean()  # Batch mean of per-sequence PPL\n    metrics[\"training_ppl\"] = training_ppl.detach().item()\n\n    # Also log log-ppl for easier analysis (avoids exponential scale)\n    metrics[\"training_log_ppl\"] = (-mean_log_prob_training).mean().detach().item()\n\n    # 2. Compute rollout off-policy metrics (only if rollout_log_probs available)\n    if rollout_log_prob is not None:\n        # 2a. kl: Direct estimator for KL(π_rollout || π_training)\n        # This is the standard KL divergence: E[log(π_rollout) - log(π_training)]\n        # Positive value means rollout policy is more confident than training policy\n        metrics[\"kl\"] = verl_F.masked_mean(rollout_log_prob - old_log_prob, response_mask).detach().item()\n\n        # 2b. k3_kl: K3 estimator for KL(π_rollout || π_training)\n        # More stable for small KL values using: E[exp(log_ratio) - log_ratio - 1]\n        # Formula: KL ≈ E[r - log(r) - 1] where r = π_training/π_rollout\n        log_ratio = old_log_prob - rollout_log_prob\n        k3_kl_matrix = torch.exp(log_ratio) - log_ratio - 1\n        metrics[\"k3_kl\"] = verl_F.masked_mean(k3_kl_matrix, response_mask).detach().item()\n\n        # 2c. Rollout policy perplexity\n        mean_log_prob_rollout = verl_F.masked_mean(rollout_log_prob, response_mask, axis=-1)  # (batch_size,)\n        rollout_ppl = torch.exp(-mean_log_prob_rollout).mean()  # Batch mean of per-sequence PPL\n        metrics[\"rollout_ppl\"] = rollout_ppl.detach().item()\n        metrics[\"rollout_log_ppl\"] = (-mean_log_prob_rollout).mean().detach().item()\n\n        # 2d. Log PPL difference (sequence-level perplexity difference)\n        # log_ppl_diff = mean_log_prob_rollout - mean_log_prob_training\n        # Since ppl = exp(-log_prob), we have:\n        #   log(ppl_ratio) = log(training_ppl/rollout_ppl) = log_ppl_diff\n        # Positive value means training assigns lower probability (higher PPL) than rollout\n        log_ppl_diff = mean_log_prob_rollout - mean_log_prob_training\n        metrics[\"log_ppl_diff\"] = log_ppl_diff.mean().detach().item()\n        metrics[\"log_ppl_abs_diff\"] = log_ppl_diff.abs().mean().detach().item()\n        metrics[\"log_ppl_diff_max\"] = log_ppl_diff.max().detach().item()\n        metrics[\"log_ppl_diff_min\"] = log_ppl_diff.min().detach().item()\n\n        # 2e. PPL ratio (how much higher is training PPL vs rollout PPL)\n        # Compute per-sequence ratio first, then average\n        # For numerical stability, compute in log space using log_ppl_diff\n        # Note: log_ppl_diff = log(ppl_ratio), so ppl_ratio = exp(log_ppl_diff)\n        # This is the inverse of geometric IS: ppl_ratio_i = 1 / geometric_is_i for each sequence\n        ppl_ratio = torch.exp(log_ppl_diff).mean()  # mean(exp(log_ppl_diff)) = mean(ppl_ratio_i)\n        metrics[\"ppl_ratio\"] = ppl_ratio.detach().item()\n\n        # 2f. Chi-squared divergence: χ²(π_training || π_rollout) = E_μ[ρ²] - 1\n        # where ρ = π_training / π_rollout and μ = π_rollout (rollout distribution)\n        # This measures the variance of importance sampling weights\n        # Token-level: E_token[ρ²] - 1 (averaged over all tokens)\n        log_ratio_safe = torch.clamp(log_ratio, min=-SAFETY_BOUND, max=SAFETY_BOUND)\n        rho_token = torch.exp(log_ratio_safe)  # ρ = π_training / π_rollout (token-level)\n        rho_squared_token = rho_token.square()\n        chi2_token = verl_F.masked_mean(rho_squared_token, response_mask) - 1.0\n        metrics[\"chi2_token\"] = chi2_token.detach().item()\n\n        # Sequence-level: E_seq[(Π ρ_t)²] - 1 = E_seq[exp(2 * Σ log ρ_t)] - 1\n        log_ratio_sum = verl_F.masked_sum(log_ratio, response_mask, axis=-1)  # Σ log ρ_t per sequence\n        log_ratio_sum_safe = torch.clamp(log_ratio_sum, min=-SAFETY_BOUND, max=SAFETY_BOUND)\n        rho_squared_seq = torch.exp(2.0 * log_ratio_sum_safe)  # (Π ρ_t)²\n        chi2_seq = rho_squared_seq.mean() - 1.0\n        metrics[\"chi2_seq\"] = chi2_seq.detach().item()\n\n    return metrics\n\n\ndef compute_rollout_correction_and_add_to_batch(\n    batch: DataProto, rollout_corr_config: RolloutCorrectionConfig\n) -> tuple[DataProto, dict]:\n    \"\"\"Compute rollout correction weights and apply rejection sampling.\n\n    Computes importance sampling weights to correct for off-policy issues between\n    rollout and training policies. Applies rejection sampling by modifying response_mask.\n    Always updates response_mask; conditionally adds IS weights.\n\n    Key behavior:\n    - response_mask: ALWAYS updated with rejection (RS exclusions removed from training)\n    - rollout_is_weights: Added to batch ONLY if rollout_is parameter is set\n\n    This separation ensures:\n    - Rejection works independently of IS weight application\n    - Metrics can be monitored before enabling IS weight correction\n\n    Args:\n        batch: DataProto with old_log_probs, rollout_log_probs, response_mask\n\n    Returns:\n        Tuple of (updated_batch, metrics):\n            updated_batch: Batch with modified response_mask (always) and rollout_is_weights (if enabled)\n            metrics: Dict of IS and off-policy metrics, all with \"rollout_corr/\" prefix\n\n    Note:\n        The implementation is copied from szrlee <szrlee@gmail.com>.\n    \"\"\"\n    # Get new API parameters directly from config\n    rollout_is = rollout_corr_config.get(\"rollout_is\", None)\n    rollout_is_threshold = rollout_corr_config.get(\"rollout_is_threshold\", 2.0)\n    rollout_is_batch_normalize = rollout_corr_config.get(\"rollout_is_batch_normalize\", False)\n    rollout_rs = rollout_corr_config.get(\"rollout_rs\", None)\n    rollout_rs_threshold = rollout_corr_config.get(\"rollout_rs_threshold\", None)\n\n    # Compute IS weights and get modified response_mask\n    rollout_is_weights, modified_response_mask, rollout_corr_metrics = compute_rollout_correction_and_rejection_mask(\n        old_log_prob=batch.batch[\"old_log_probs\"],\n        rollout_log_prob=batch.batch[\"rollout_log_probs\"],\n        response_mask=batch.batch[\"response_mask\"],\n        rollout_is=rollout_is,\n        rollout_is_threshold=rollout_is_threshold,\n        rollout_is_batch_normalize=rollout_is_batch_normalize,\n        rollout_rs=rollout_rs,\n        rollout_rs_threshold=rollout_rs_threshold,\n    )\n\n    # ALWAYS update response_mask with rejection applied\n    batch.batch[\"response_mask\"] = modified_response_mask\n\n    # Add IS weights to batch if computed\n    if rollout_is_weights is not None:\n        batch = batch.union(rollout_is_weights)\n\n    return batch, rollout_corr_metrics\n\n\ndef compute_rollout_corr_metrics_from_logprobs(\n    log_prob: torch.Tensor,\n    rollout_log_prob: torch.Tensor,\n    response_mask: torch.Tensor,\n) -> dict[str, float]:\n    \"\"\"Compute rollout correction metrics from log probabilities during training.\n\n    This function is used in the actor to compute metrics using the CURRENT policy\n    log probabilities versus rollout log probabilities, allowing tracking of the\n    off-policy gap as training progresses.\n\n    It computes off-policy diagnostic metrics (KL, PPL, χ²) from log probabilities.\n\n    Args:\n        log_prob: Current policy log probabilities, shape (batch_size, seq_length)\n        rollout_log_prob: Rollout policy log probabilities, shape (batch_size, seq_length)\n        response_mask: Valid token mask, shape (batch_size, seq_length)\n\n    Returns:\n        Dictionary of metrics with \"rollout_corr/\" prefix\n    \"\"\"\n    # Compute off-policy diagnostic metrics\n    offpolicy_metrics = compute_offpolicy_metrics(\n        old_log_prob=log_prob,\n        rollout_log_prob=rollout_log_prob,\n        response_mask=response_mask,\n    )\n\n    # Add rollout_corr/ prefix to all metrics\n    metrics_with_prefix = {}\n    for key, value in offpolicy_metrics.items():\n        if isinstance(value, torch.Tensor):\n            metrics_with_prefix[f\"rollout_corr/{key}\"] = value.item()\n        else:\n            metrics_with_prefix[f\"rollout_corr/{key}\"] = value\n\n    return metrics_with_prefix\n\n\ndef apply_bypass_mode(\n    batch: DataProto,\n    rollout_corr_config: Optional[RolloutCorrectionConfig] = None,\n    policy_loss_config: PolicyLossConfig = None,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"\n    Setup bypass mode: Use rollout_log_probs as old_log_probs.\n\n    Bypass mode skips expensive actor forward pass for old_log_prob computation\n    by setting old_log_probs = rollout_log_probs (2 policies instead of 3).\n\n    Uses compute_policy_loss_bypass_mode() which supports:\n    - loss_type=\"ppo_clip\" (default): PPO clipped objective (IS handled by ratio)\n    - loss_type=\"reinforce\": REINFORCE with explicit IS weights\n\n    Both loss types benefit from rejection sampling (RS) which masks out-of-distribution samples.\n\n    Note:\n        The implementation is copied from szrlee <szrlee@gmail.com>.\n    \"\"\"\n    from omegaconf import open_dict\n\n    if \"rollout_log_probs\" not in batch.batch:\n        raise ValueError(\n            \"bypass_mode=True requires rollout_log_probs in batch. \"\n            \"Ensure rollout worker is configured to calculate_log_probs=true.\"\n        )\n\n    # Use rollout log probs as old log probs (zero-cost substitution)\n    batch.batch[\"old_log_probs\"] = batch.batch[\"rollout_log_probs\"]\n\n    with open_dict(policy_loss_config):\n        # Pass rollout_correction config to actor for loss computation and metrics\n        policy_loss_config[\"rollout_correction\"] = rollout_corr_config\n        # Always use bypass_mode loss function which handles both loss_types\n        policy_loss_config[\"loss_mode\"] = \"bypass_mode\"\n", "numLines": 1143, "startLine": 1, "totalLines": 1143}}
